dimensions.assessment: Directly impacts eligible U.S. Customs and Border Protection Officers who received tentative offers prior to July 6, 2008, as well as CBP and OPM personnel.
dimensions.evidence: any individual who received a tentative offer of employment as a U.S. Customs and Border Protection Officer before July 6, 2008; and entered into duty... on or after July 6, 2008

dimensions.assessment: Provides retroactive annuity adjustments, minimum annuity amounts, mandatory retirement exemptions, and possible maximum entry age waivers for affected officers.
dimensions.evidence: are entitled to... the minimum annuity amount required... and an exemption from mandatory retirement... including a retroactive annuity adjustment

dimensions.assessment: Involves retroactive annuity adjustments and administrative costs for CBP and OPM, though specific total cost figures are not provided.
dimensions.evidence: including a retroactive annuity adjustment for Eligible Individuals who retired before the date of the enactment of this Act.

dimensions.assessment: Directs specific federal agencies to adjust retirement classifications, issue guidance, waive certain age limits, and conduct a GAO review of hiring practices.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Homeland Security shall create a list of all Eligible Individuals... and provide the Director of the Office of Personnel Management with all of the information

dimensions.assessment: Permanent individual retirement adjustments and a one-time GAO review and report deadline within 18 months.
dimensions.evidence: not later than 18 months after the date of the enactment of this Act, shall submit a report

missing_information: Total number of eligible individuals and total financial cost of the retroactive annuity adjustments.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill corrects retirement and annuity benefits for specific U.S. Customs and Border Protection Officers who received tentative offers before July 6, 2008, requiring agency lists, OPM corrections, and a GAO review.
